newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern Africa miners urged to unite.
newsitem.headline: Southern Africa miners urged to unite.

text.p: Miners in the Southern African region must unite to protect themselves against retrenchments as mining houses invest more and more in East and West Africa, a mining federation president said.

"The re-organisation will give us a greater collective strength to make our imprint on the economic and political development of Southern Africa and world-wide," James Motlatsi, president of the Southern Africa Miners' Federation, said in Windhoek on Monday.

Motlatsi, who is also president of the International Chemical, Energy, Mining and General Workers Federation, urged miners to decide on a course of action, even if it meant taking industrial action against mining houses, which he said were the opponents of miners throughout Southern Africa.

"They (mining houses) are interested only in making profits... I believe that their long-term profit-making strategies entail running down their long-standing operations in Southern Africa while they get easy profits from mining in West Africa and elsewhere.

"They will retrench in the profitable mines but will mothball the marginal ones where the mineral deposits are costly to reach. As compensation they will skim profits from mining rich deposits in Ghana, Mali, Senegal and Guinea," he said.
Motlatsi cited Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd.
"We should meet to consider whether we should lobby the governments, approach the Organisation of African Unity and even consider taking industrial action to oppose them," he said.
